draft.title: Geometric constructions as steps
card: A construction draws a shape using only a compass and an unmarked ruler. It is a list of steps in a set order, like an algorithm.
To bisect an angle, which means to cut it into two equal angles: first, put the compass point on the vertex and draw an arc across both arms.
Next, put the compass point on each arc crossing in turn and draw two arcs with the same radius that cross inside the angle. Last, draw a line from the vertex through that crossing.
Followed in order, the steps work for any angle. Changing the order or skipping a step can break the result.
draft.remember: A construction is an ordered set of steps that works every time.

a.q: What is the first step when bisecting an angle with a compass and ruler?
opts: Draw an arc across both arms, centred on the vertex
Draw a line through the middle of the angle
Draw two crossing arcs inside the angle
Measure the angle with a protractor
a.why: The first step is an arc centred on the vertex that crosses both arms. The crossing arcs inside the angle come after, and the final line is drawn last. A construction does not use a protractor.

b.q: Sam bisects an angle but draws the final line before the two crossing arcs. Why can he not finish the construction correctly?
opts: The crossing point that fixes the line is not drawn yet
The compass was not set to the size of the angle
Angles can only be bisected by measuring them
The steps can be done in any order
b.why: The line goes through the vertex and the crossing of the two arcs, so the crossing must exist first. Order matters in a construction. The compass radius is not set to the angle size, and no measuring is needed.
b.clue: What does the last line need to pass through?

a.best: Draw an arc across both arms, centred on the vertex

b.best: The crossing point that fixes the line is not drawn yet
